Definition: of Hebrew origin (H5514); Sina (i.e. Sinai), a mountain in Arabia:--Sina.
BiblicalUsage: Sina is Sinai, the mountain in Arabia where the angel appeared to Moses in a flame of fire in a bush, and where Moses received the lively oracles to give to Israel. Paul reads it as an allegory: the mount Sinai genders to bondage, and stands for the covenant of law beside the covenant of promise.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Sinai is the mountain of law and of glory in the same breath, and I hold that the fire that burned and did not consume is the God who gives His law and keeps His promise.
